title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يشارك في ملتقى علماء أهل السنة لمواجهة الاستبداد وسفك الدماء
title_en: The Sheikh Takes Part in the Forum of the Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah to Confront Tyranny and the Shedding of Blood
body_ar:
افتتح صباح اليوم السبت 08 – 08 - 2015 الموافق الموافق 23 \24 شوال 1436هـ بالعاصمة التركية اسطنبول المؤتمر العالمي لعلماء أهل السنة المنظم تحت شعار (ملتقى علماء أهل السنة لمواجهة الاستبداد وسفك الدماء ) الذي تقيمه رابطة علماء أهل السنة بالتعاون مع عدد من الهيئات والروابط و المنظمات الإسلامية و بحضور علماء يمثلون أكثر من خمس و عشرين دولة

و قد تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو ـ حفظه الله تعالى ـ في بداية المؤتمر عن دور العلماء في محاربة الاستبداد مذكرا إياهم بالوعد الذي أخذه الله تعالى عليهم بأن يبينوا هذا الدين و ألا يكتمونه

مشددا على أن الأمة تواجه هجمة شرسة من الغزاة الخارجين يتقدم عبدة الصليب و الصهاينة الحاقدين يؤازرهم المدد الداخلي من الحكام المستبدين الطغاة و الروافض الذين كانوا عبر التاريخ ضد هذه الأمة في كل توجهاتها و مع أعدائها و كذلك التطرف الذي جاب مشارق هذه الأمة و مغاربها إذ هو ناشئ عن اختفاء العلماء ليظهر الرويبضات يحملون الراية و يتجمع عليهم بقصد الصالح و الطالح كل من يريد التغيير سواء كان صادقا في نيته أو غير ذلك

و قد أكد فضيلة الشيخ أن العلماء تحت خمس رقابات و عليهم أن يتبينوا ذلك فالرقابة الأولى رقابة الله تعالى، والرقابة الثانية رقابة الرسول الشهيد صلى الله عليه وسلم، و الرقابة الثالثة رقابة الملائكة الكرام الكاتبين فمع كل إنسان منا 21 ملكا ( و إن عليكم لحافظين كراما كاتبين يعلمون ما تفعلون ) ، والرقابة الرابعة رقابة المؤمنين (وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون) ، و الرقابة الخامسة رقابة الإنسان على نفسه (بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة )

ويهدف المؤتمر الذي تستمر أعماله لمدة يومين (08 _ 09 من شهر أغسطس الجاري ) إلى حشد العلماء وإبراز دورهم في مواجهة كل أشكال الظلم والاستبداد وسفك الدماء التى تستهدف أهل السنة في جميع أقطار العالم، والتباحث حول الأمور التالية:
- سبل توحيد أهل السنة أمام أي مشروع يستهدف الهوية السنية.
- إصدار الحكم الشرعي للجرائم التي ترتكبها سلطة الانقلاب بمصر.

body_en:
This Saturday morning, 08–08–2015, corresponding to 23/24 Shawwal 1436 AH, the World Conference of the Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah (the Sunnis) opened in the Turkish capital Istanbul, convened under the banner 'The Forum of the Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah to Confront Tyranny and the Shedding of Blood'. It is held by the Association of Scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah in cooperation with a number of Islamic bodies, leagues and organisations, and attended by scholars representing more than twenty-five countries.

At the opening of the conference His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) spoke about the role of the scholars in combating tyranny, reminding them of the pledge that God the Exalted took from them: that they would make this religion plain and would not conceal it.

He stressed that the community faces a ferocious assault from invaders from without, at the head of whom are the worshippers of the cross and the spiteful Zionists, supported from within by tyrannical, despotic rulers and by the Rāfiḍah, who throughout history have stood against this community in every direction it has taken and have sided with its enemies; and likewise by the extremism that has ranged across the east and the west of this community — for that extremism arises from the disappearance of the scholars, so that the contemptible ignoramuses (al-ruwaybiḍāt) come forward carrying the banner, and everyone who wants change gathers around them, the sound and the corrupt alike, whether sincere in intention or otherwise.

The Sheikh affirmed that the scholars stand under five forms of scrutiny, and that they must be clear about this. The first is the scrutiny of God the Exalted. The second is the scrutiny of the Messenger who bears witness, God bless him and grant him peace. The third is the scrutiny of the noble angels who record, for with each one of us there are twenty-one angels: {And indeed, there are keepers over you, noble scribes, who know what you do} (Sūrat al-Infiṭār 82:10–12). The fourth is the scrutiny of the believers: {And say: Act, for God will see your work, and His Messenger, and the believers} (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:105). And the fifth is a person's scrutiny of himself: {Rather, man is a clear witness against himself} (Sūrat al-Qiyāmah 75:14).

The conference, whose proceedings run for two days (08–09 of this month of August), aims to rally the scholars and to bring out their role in confronting every form of injustice, tyranny and bloodshed directed at Ahl al-Sunnah in all the lands of the world, and to deliberate on the following matters:
- The ways to unite Ahl al-Sunnah in the face of any project that targets the Sunni identity.
- Issuing the ruling of the Sharia on the crimes committed by the coup authority in Egypt.
The practical measures the scholars will take to confront tyranny and the shedding of blood

flags.arabic: يتقدم عبدة الصليب و الصهاينة الحاقدين يؤازرهم المدد الداخلي من الحكام المستبدين الطغاة و الروافض
flags.context: the Sheikh's opening address, as reported by the site
options: at the head of whom are the worshippers of the cross and the spiteful Zionists, supported from within by tyrannical, despotic rulers and by the Rāfiḍah
led by the Crusaders and the rancorous Zionists, backed internally by despotic tyrant rulers and by the Shia
translate the polemical epithets and gloss each one in a note
flags.note: EDITORIALLY SENSITIVE. 'عبدة الصليب' (worshippers of the cross) and 'الروافض' (the Rāfiḍah) are polemical epithets for Christians and for Twelver Shia respectively. Rendering them neutrally as 'Christians' and 'the Shia' would soften the Arabic; rendering them literally carries them into English, where they read as sectarian incitement and may engage hate-speech law in some jurisdictions. Translated literally here, as the style guide requires, and referred up. Note also that this is the SITE'S REPORT of what the Sheikh said, not a text he wrote.

flags.arabic: إصدار الحكم الشرعي للجرائم التي ترتكبها سلطة الانقلاب بمصر
flags.context: the second item on the conference agenda
options: Issuing the ruling of the Sharia on the crimes committed by the coup authority in Egypt
Pronouncing the Sharia judgement upon the offences of the coup regime in Egypt
flags.note: EDITORIALLY SENSITIVE. This is a conference agenda item, not a ruling of the Sheikh's, but in English it reads as a scholarly body preparing a verdict against a sitting government. Publishing it may carry legal exposure in Egypt and elsewhere. It is the conference organisers' wording, and the display must not attribute it to the Sheikh.

flags.arabic: الرسول الشهيد صلى الله عليه وسلم
flags.context: الرقابة الثانية رقابة الرسول الشهيد صلى الله عليه وسلم
options: the Messenger who is a witness over the community
flags.note: MISTRANSLATION RISK: شهيد here is 'witness', in the Qur'anic sense of the Prophet as witness over his community ('and We brought you as a witness over these'), not 'martyr'. Rendering it 'the martyred Messenger' would be a doctrinal error.

flags.context: the third form of scrutiny, the recording angels
options: twenty angels, the figure in the better-known report
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, RECORDED NOT FIXED (house rule 11): the widely cited report gives twenty angels, ten by day and ten by night. The source here says twenty-one. It has been translated as it stands and not corrected; whether the extra angel is the Sheikh's own reckoning or a reporting slip cannot be settled from the text.

flags.arabic: و يتجمع عليهم بقصد الصالح و الطالح كل من يريد التغيير
flags.context: the clause following the mention of al-ruwaybiḍāt
options: everyone who wants change gathers around them, the sound and the corrupt alike
everyone who wants change gathers around them, intending good or ill
the sound and the corrupt alike resort to them deliberately
flags.note: The Arabic is syntactically loose as transcribed and 'بقصد' can attach either to the people gathering or to their intention. The reading chosen is the one the following clause ('whether sincere in intention or otherwise') supports.

options: read as: corresponding to 23/24 Shawwal 1436 AH
flags.note: TWO SOURCE DEFECTS in one clause, preserved in body_ar and omitted from body_en (house rule 11): 'الموافق' is printed twice, and the backslash in '23 \24' is an addslashes artifact standing for a solidus between the two Hijri dates. This is the corpus-wide escaping defect and should be cleaned globally, not in this record.

translator_notes: This is a news report about the Sheikh's participation, written by the site, not a text authored by the Sheikh. His words are reported indirectly throughout and the English preserves that indirection.

The three Qur'anic references are supplied by the translator; the source quotes the verses without reference. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
الرويبضة is the term of the hadith 'the contemptible man who speaks on the affairs of the public'; the plural الرويبضات is kept with a gloss rather than paraphrased away.
The stray pair of quotation marks after the heading of the list of participating bodies is in the source and has been left out of the English.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date of composition.
dec: Carries polemical epithets for Christians and for Twelver Shia, rendered literally as the style guide requires.
